instructions: In a jar or measuring cup, stir together the mentsuyu and 1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp of water. Put it in the freezer to chill while you do the rest.
Thinly slice the scallions. Peel the ginger and grate it. Crack each egg into its own small cup or ramekin.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil for the udon. Bring a medium pot of water to a gentle simmer in a second pot and add the vinegar.

Stir the simmering water to make a slow swirl. Slide in 2 eggs and cook for 2 1/2 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are still runny. Lift them out with a slotted spoon onto a plate. Repeat with the other 2 eggs.
Boil the udon in the large pot for the time on the pack, about 1 to 2 minutes for frozen. Stir with chopsticks to separate the noodles.
Drain the noodles and rinse them under cold running water, rubbing them gently, until they're cool. Drain well.
Divide the noodles among 4 bowls. Pour about 1/3 cup of the chilled sauce over each bowl.
Top each bowl with a poached egg, scallions, ginger and a pinch of the bonito flakes. Serve right away.
method_notes: Bukkake udon has no version with 20 ratings: Chef JA Cooks has 5 stars from 4, Pickled Plum and Cooking with Dog none. It leads with Chef JA Cooks for the 2 to 1 mentsuyu to water sauce and the cold-rinsed noodles. The poached egg and the toppings come from Pickled Plum. The sauce is strong by design, and 'bukkake' means it is poured over. Check your mentsuyu bottle: this assumes a 3x concentrate; for a different strength, dilute to the ratio on the label for dipping noodles.
